# ChatGPT image route

A user who asks to generate on their ChatGPT or Codex subscription without choosing another tool gets `chatgpt:image`: it runs their own signed-in Codex CLI on their ChatGPT plan (it uses the plan's Codex usage, then any OpenAI credits on their account; never Voyager credits) and keeps the image as a tracked job in the project. Use it only when the user asked for their subscription, and say once that it uses their plan.

Image generation uses the account your Codex CLI is signed into; if the user requests an account switch, run `codex logout`, then `codex login` with the other account (use the same `CODEX_HOME` if set). Accounts added under Connectors → Providers are for chat, not image generation.

If they want no spend beyond the plan, run `models.estimate` first and relay `planUsage.message` (the plan's used share, any OpenAI credits, and `zeroExtraSpend`: `plan_only`, `credits_may_pay` or `unknown`), then add `"planOnly": true` to the input: the job runs on the plan while it has usage left, whether or not the account has OpenAI credits, and never falls back to credits. Voyager refuses it before anything is sent (`PLAN_ONLY`, nothing spent) once Codex reports the plan's usage used up, and stops it with `PLAN_ONLY` if the usage runs out while it runs (a request already under way then may still draw on OpenAI credits, which OpenAI has no setting to stop). On `PLAN_ONLY`, tell the user the plan's usage is used up; run without `planOnly` only if they accept OpenAI credits paying, and never retry it unchanged.

Read `voyager models show chatgpt:image --json` for reference limits and accepted inputs; select the most important references or combine them into a contact sheet. Input: `{"prompt": "...", "images": [{"$file": "ref.png"}], "size": "square|landscape|portrait", "background": "transparent"}`; estimate the actual request for timing and payer.

If it says Codex is not signed in, pass on its message and the exact login command it gives (it can be a full path to Codex); Voyager's own ChatGPT sign-in in the chat never makes these images, so that user still signs the Codex CLI in with ChatGPT once. Only when that route is unavailable, use your own built-in image tool if you have one, copy its saved file into the project and present it; never after a `chatgpt:image` job failed or may have run.

# The user's pets

Voyager users can hatch a pet: a small companion that lives in the corner of the app. Each pet is
a folder in the creative home, `<home>/pets/<id>/`, where `<home>` is the creative home reported in
`voyager doctor --json`. When the user mentions their pet, or a companion by name ("put Mochi in
the thumbnail"), find it there; never ask them to upload it.

## What a pet folder holds

- `pet.json`: `name`, `species`, `description` (what the user asked for), `kind` (creature,
  person, robot or object; absent means anything), `style` (plush, clay, pixel, sticker, anime,
  watercolor, 3d, cartoon, comic, figurine, low-poly), `customStyle` (the look in the user's own
  words; when present it wins over `style`), `temperament`, `personality` (the user's own words,
  when given), `bio`, `accent` (CSS colour), and `sheet`.
- `sheet.file` (e.g. `look-mv21j1vs.png`): the current look, a 3×3 expression sheet of the same
  character on a transparent background, poses in order idle, happy, thinking, working,
  celebrating, sad, sleeping, surprised, waving. `sheet.frames` gives each pose's box in pixels.
- `idle.png`: the idle pose alone, cropped, transparent. The best single reference.
- `looks` in `pet.json` lists earlier looks; use the current `sheet.file` unless asked otherwise.

Find a pet by name: read each `pets/*/pet.json` and match `name` case-insensitively. `pets/state.json`
names the active pet (`activeId`) when the user says "my pet".

## Putting the pet in an image or video

Use `idle.png` as the identity reference (add the sheet when a pose matters, e.g. the waving
cell for a greeting) and say in the prompt that this exact character must appear, keeping its
colours, markings and accessories, in the pet's own look (`customStyle` when present, else
`style`) unless the user asks for another. A `person` pet stays a person: keep their likeness.
Pet folders belong to the app: read them, never edit or delete them. Write generated work to the
project as usual.

# Soul identity training

For the same real person across many stills, only with their consent and a
Higgsfield sign-in: `voyager soul list`, or `voyager soul estimate` then
`voyager soul train` from 5–20 photos of them after the user's explicit yes;
generate with `higgsfield:text2image_soul_v2` and the Soul's id as
`custom_reference_id`. It bills their Higgsfield plan, never Voyager credits.

---
name: make-image
description: "Generate or edit raster pictures with Voyager models; cut out, upscale or vectorize an existing image."
applications:
  - id: moda
    role: primary
voyager:
  schemaVersion: 1
  design: optional
---

## Make an image with a point of view

Left to its defaults, an image becomes a polished subject in flattering light, full of detail
and empty of intent. Refuse that. You are the best image maker on this job, and the bar is a
picture people remember. Find what the viewer should notice or feel, then make framing, light,
gesture, texture and color carry that idea. Choose a viewpoint with a reason to exist. Let
specific details tell the story instead of piling style adjectives onto a generic scene. In an
edit, see what gives the original its identity and make the change belong to that same world.
Look at the result as a small image, then inspect the focal area and its relationship to the
references. If the finish is impressive but the picture says nothing, push the image further.

Honor explicit tool, model, size and quality; otherwise use these defaults.
If the user explicitly chooses another tool or website, use it; the Voyager generation
commands below apply to Voyager routes.
For an active design direction in context or `voyager direction resolve --json`,
use its palette, type and logo treatment per
[design direction](../brand-kit/references/directions.md). Generation validates inputs
and saves provenance; never create request/result files.

## Source real subjects

For a real subject, use the first usable source: the user's asset (brief,
attachments, project, brand kit or a named path, never a disk search), then the
subject's official source or open libraries/stock, then generation when exact
structure or labels are not required, then a hand-built depiction labeled
schematic. The user's explicitly requested version wins; a guessed asset type
is not such a request. Abstract or invented subjects are made freely. Follow the
runtime's likeness, licensing and factual-claim boundaries.

## Recurring characters

For a character across stills or a video's keyframes, follow
[Project Elements](../make-ai-video/SKILL.md#keeping-shots-in-one-world): reuse a card or make a hero
portrait, full body and fixed description with `cast.create`. A card is ready as
soon as it exists. A card's `style` says
how its references look, not how a shot must look: choose each shot's look in
the prompt. Use `cast.models`
for image routing and pass top-level `cast: ["mara"]` plus project `directory`
on every estimate/run with the character, including edits and retakes. The
adapter attaches photos and returns their labels and descriptions in the estimate.
Write each visible element’s identity (people, places and props) in your prompt using those labels; you may choose refs
by role or filename. Additional style/composition/edit inputs stay explicit. Visually compare the result with its references. For a paid second opinion, use `voyager cast check` (Voyager credits or a connected Google key); generation does not run it automatically.

The Elements panel needs a project thread: open the side panel's **+** launcher and
choose **Elements** (or press **K** there). In a standalone thread, choose a thread
in the project first.

## Finish the layout

Generation uses the chosen route, billed to its account. When the brief needs more
than the raw image (exact words, a logo, a layout, several sizes, print or
vector output), generate the picture without lettering, then finish its
lettering and layout as
[make-static-graphic](../make-static-graphic/SKILL.md) describes and
use the user’s named tool or saved creative preference. A cover with a title is
such a brief; "an image of a cat" or a photo edit is not.

A thumbnail may heighten the real story; it should not imply events or
results the video never contains.

For best/latest model comparisons, unfamiliar edits, or requirements the defaults
may not meet, see [Image models](#image-models).

A local model the user named ("on Local" or "on this computer") is available if appropriate: `voyager models run "local:FLUX.2 klein 4B" --prompt "a red fox" --json` (its name or id) runs it free and returns the image, with no lookup or estimate first.

## Generate or edit

Default: **Nano Banana 2.1**, one 1K image, square unless another format is requested.
It runs through Voyager credits, a FAL key or a Google key. A user who wants GPT Image on their own OpenAI key needs a custom connector (see custom-connectors); otherwise GPT Image runs through FAL or Higgsfield. For images on a ChatGPT or Codex subscription, use `chatgpt:image` only when requested; see [ChatGPT image route](references/chatgpt-image.md) for account, plan-only spend and reference limits. Voyager falls back across the user's providers by itself on credit, sign-in or outage failures; never resubmit on another model or provider yourself (for a content-filter rejection, follow [policy rejections](../make-ai-video/SKILL.md#generate-check-deliver)).

```sh
voyager models run --input - --json <<'JSON'
{
  "model": "nano-banana-2.1",
  "prompt": "A friendly cat in warm natural light",
  "parameters": { "aspectRatio": "1:1", "resolution": "1K" }
}
JSON
```

Write prompts with the model's rules in [Still images](#still-images) below.

On a billing refusal, follow the runtime instructions’ paid generation policy.

For edits, add `references: ["reference.png"]` alongside
`prompt` and `parameters`. Give each reference one role in the prompt (identity,
style, composition or the image to edit). When the user asked for a style (line
art, a sketch, a style key), a photo reference supplies identity only and the
requested style wins; check the result for drift toward the photo before you
accept it, as [the style key rule](../make-ai-video/SKILL.md#keeping-shots-in-one-world)
describes. The preset sends references with the edit request.
Use `voyager models show nano-banana-2.1 --json` for reference limits, ratios and resolutions.

For consented identity training on Higgsfield, see [Soul](references/soul.md) for
training inputs, identity IDs and billing.

Alternative: **GPT Image 2.5 Flare** for explicit GPT Image requests or transparent
output. Use this native envelope (`model` is a JSON field, not `--endpoint`):

```sh
voyager models run --input - --json <<'JSON'
{
  "model": "openai/gpt-image-2.5/flare/text-to-image",
  "input": {
    "prompt": "A blue ceramic vase in soft studio light",
    "image_size": "square_hd",
    "quality": "medium",
    "num_images": 1
  }
}
JSON
```

For transparency add `background: "transparent"` inside `input`. For edits, replace
`/text-to-image` with `/edit` and add `image_urls: [{"$file":"reference.png"}]` inside
`input`. Never mix native `input` with shortcut `prompt`, `references`, or `parameters`.
`cast` and `directory` remain top-level on either envelope; the adapter adds
the card's identity refs, including for native edit requests.
Pass a short top-level `title` naming the idea (`"title": "Hero shot"`) and reuse it for
retakes of that idea, so its takes share a file name (`takes/hero-shot-take-02.png`).
Use `voyager models show ENDPOINT --json` for unfamiliar options or validation
errors.

## Image models

Nano Banana 2.1 stays the default for general stills and reference-guided edits. FLUX.3 Klein suits quick drafts, text edits, relights, product placement and variations; not fixed-style storyboard frames, several references or pose changes. GPT Image 2.5 Flare suits explicit GPT Image requests or transparent output.

For “best/latest”, unfamiliar capabilities, or uncertain quality tradeoffs, use available web search to check current official model releases and endpoint docs. Translate the brief into short capability terms or synonyms for `voyager models list`; use `voyager models show MODEL --refresh --json` for the exact variant and `voyager models docs MODEL --json` for dated provider documentation.

For a model the user names or an unusual job, `voyager models list --query "image" --json` covers the long tail and returns endpoint IDs; query a family by name and use `--status all` to include deprecated endpoints. Use `voyager models show MODEL --json` for inputs and limits, `voyager models estimate` for price, speed and payer, and `voyager models docs MODEL --json` for vendor documentation.

| Need | Candidates and prompting distinctions |
| --- | --- |
| General image generation, transparency, iterative edits | GPT Image 2.5 Flare generation or edit: explicit alpha, edit mask and multiple edit references (check the operation’s schema). |
| Intricate hero art and demanding revisions | GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst generation or edit: extra precision with longer generation times. |
| General stills and reference-guided edits (default) | Nano Banana 2.1. |
| The same real person across many stills | Higgsfield Soul 2.0, with that person's consent; follow [Soul](references/soul.md). |
| Inexpensive drafts or multi-reference FLUX edits | Klein 4B, Klein 9B edit, FLUX 2 Max edit; inspect 9B or Max for different tradeoffs. |
| Layouts, reference composition, text-rich graphics | Seedream 5 Pro edit or Ideogram 4. Seedream silently keeps the last references when given too many: inspect its limit before attaching them. Ideogram was trained on JSON captions, so with prompt expansion off write the JSON caption. |
| Editing part of a large photo while every other pixel stays exact | Ideogram 4.5 Precise Edit, `ideogram:precise-edit` on Voyager credits: images up to 8192×8192, returned at the same size. Input `{prompt, image, mask?, context_window?, quality?}`; the mask is white where the edit goes, black to keep. See `voyager models show ideogram:precise-edit`. |
| Scalable vectors and consistent brand illustrations | Recraft vector, create style, style vector. |
| Moodboard-led style exploration | Krea 2 Medium or Large: creativity control, weighted style references and a moodboard. |

Use GPT Image 2.5's full Flare/Sunburst operation path, not the bare family name.

## Still images

The exclusion syntax differs by model, below.

### GPT Image 2.5 Flare and Sunburst

- Exclusions go in the prompt: "Render the tagline exactly once … No extra text, no watermarks, no unrelated logos."
- Edits: "change only X" plus the preserved list. Repeated edits drift: restate it each time, and
  composite into the original where pixels must not change.
- References: "Place the dog from image 2 into the setting of image 1 … Do not change anything else."
- Transparency: ask for an isolated subject in the prompt, set `background: "transparent"`, output PNG or WebP,
  and check the alpha (hair, glass, shadows). A painted checkerboard is not transparency.
- Read `voyager models show openai/gpt-image-2.5/flare/edit --json` (or the chosen Sunburst operation) for quality defaults.

### Nano Banana 2.1, 2 and Pro

- Exclusions as the wanted state: "an empty, deserted street with no signs of traffic", not "no cars".
- Edit: "Using the provided image, change only the [element] to [new]. Keep everything else exactly the same."
  Compose: "Take the [element] from image 1 and place it on the [element] from image 2."

### FLUX.2 (Klein, Pro, Max)

- No negative prompts: describe only what you want.
- Hex colours bound to an object: "the logo text 'ACME' in color #FF5733". JSON prompts work too.
- Multi-reference: say what each image supplies ("use the wood from image 5 for the base").

### Seedream 5 Pro

- On-image text in double quotes. Up to about 600 English words; longer prompts lose detail.
- Several images: say what each contributes; Fal's examples call them "Figure 1", ByteDance's "Image 1".
  More than 10 inputs silently keeps the last 10; `voyager models show bytedance/seedream/v5/pro/edit --json` has the limits.

### Ideogram 4

Trained on JSON captions. Plain prompts need expansion (`expansion_model` Medium or Large).
With `None`, write `high_level_description`, `style_description` (lighting, medium,
colours) and `compositional_deconstruction` (background and elements;
text elements carry the exact `text`). Read `voyager models show fal-ai/ideogram/v4/generate --json` for palette limits.

## Media utilities

`voyager media cutout FRAME --prompt "the left-most car" --output located.png` keeps every confident match, so name exactly one instance; `voyager media crop-alpha located.png --output crop.png --json` reports its `box` (x, y, width, height in frame pixels).

`voyager media crop-alpha input.png --output cropped.png --json` trims existing transparency to the visible pixels (local, free).

Raster logo or icon to SVG: Illustrator's Image Trace when the user names
Illustrator; otherwise `voyager models run` with `fal-ai/recraft/vectorize` and
`input: {"image_url": {"$file": "PATH"}}`. For an editable logo or exact geometry, author it in make-static-graphic;
an explicitly requested generative logo experiment can use an image model.

## Wait and deliver

Use the returned `result.job.id`:

```sh
voyager jobs wait JOB_ID --timeout 60 --json
```

For several images, start every one first, then wait on all their job IDs in one
call (`voyager jobs wait ID1 ID2 ... --all --timeout 60 --json`, which returns
`result.jobs`); never wait on them one at a time. If that wait ends on a billing wall
(`QUOTA`) with other images still pending (`error.details.pending`), ask how to finish first;
unless the answer is an upgrade or credits, cancel those with one
`voyager jobs cancel ID1 ID2 ... --json`: they would meet the same wall.

`result.reused: true` is the job of an identical earlier request: nothing new runs
and nothing more is charged. Tell the user plainly ("That exact image already
exists; reusing it.") and use `--fresh` only if they want a new take.

Check `result.job.state`, not just `ok`. Completed waits include paths in
`result.job.outputs`; no extra `jobs result` call is required. On timeout, wait
on the same job. Recover collection
failures on the existing job; investigate uncertain submissions before paying again.
While `job.error.details.reason` is `provider_confirming`, keep waiting on the same job
(Voyager rechecks it with backoff). After `provider_lost`, stop polling the old job:
submit once with `--fresh` only when its error says it was not charged; if it was
charged or Moda cannot tell, tell the user and ask before a new take.

Return an absolute local file link; never paste signed URLs or image bytes.
For authentication, unfamiliar models/commands, or
recovery, run the command's `--help` and `voyager doctor --json`.

## Color And Brand

For any named brand, logo, brand kit or requested brand match, and for color contrast.

- Real brand facts win over inferred treatment. Use the selected snapshot's
  palette, type and supplied logo files, unmodified and in their documented
  variants.

- Exceptions are recorded, not improvised: they live in the brand snapshot's
  `overrides.md` or the active design direction.

- Say what was substituted or unavailable instead of claiming full brand
  fidelity, and name the kit used in the handoff.

### Using a kit

Read the project's brand snapshot (normally `brand/BRAND.md`, with `kit.json`
for tokens and the guides it links) as the `brand-kit` skill describes, and only
the fields the deliverable needs. Work for a website reads its site kit,
`brand/sites/<host>/kit.md`: take colours from `palette.json`, load the faces in
`fonts/` as local fonts, and place logos from `logos/` in the variant `kit.md`
marks transparent.

### Logos and marks

Inspect a logo file before placing it: pick the variant that suits the ground.
Verify a downloaded official mark against its published hash when one is given.
Partner and platform marks are sourced separately and never replace the user's
own brand as the design's identity.

### Color and contrast

A gradient word must stay readable at every stop; on
a dark ground, end on the lightest accent, never on dark purple, navy or black.

### After compression

Judge color in the encoded file, not the composition: faint decoration (glows,
patterns, watermark shapes) can vanish once encoded.

## Locate And Safe Areas

For placing labels, callouts and boxes on real images or moving subjects, and platform safe areas.

- Keep essential text and marks inside the platform's safe area (the `edit-video` skill's `references/social-safe-areas.md` lists them).

### Locate before you annotate

- **Segment it.** `voyager media cutout FRAME --prompt "the red car" --output
  located.png` (SAM 3, metered, about half a cent) keeps every confident match,
  so name exactly one instance ("the left-most car"). Then `voyager media
  crop-alpha located.png --output crop.png --json` reports its `box` (x, y,
  width, height in frame pixels) at no cost.

## Tool Choice

For which tool builds the work and how to drive it: batch when mechanical, step when perceptual.

- **A tool the user names in this conversation wins.** Otherwise the
  `<voyager_creative_preferences>` block (a saved tool, or an app switched off)
  overrides everything below.

- **See what's available** in the `<voyager_environment>` block: its `Ready`
  and `Installed` lines list the apps on this machine. Outside the app (Claude
  Code, Codex), run `voyager capabilities --json`.

- **Parse JSON from stdout only.** Do not merge stderr with `2>&1` when parsing
  `--json` output; progress notices and live tool output go to stderr.

- **Defaults when the choice is yours** (the job is on Agent decides). Apps the
  user switched off remain unavailable.

  | Category              | Default                                                                                                                                         | Installed app: only when named, already in use, or its project file is asked for | Notes                                                                              |
  | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Motion                | Remotion, then HyperFrames                                                                                                                      | After Effects                                                                    | Manim for equations                                                                |
  | Editing               | Voyager's video engine when ready, for transcript cuts, B-roll over speech, montages and ducked beds; FFmpeg via edit-video for the rest        | Resolve, Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro                                             | Final Cut Pro gets an FCPXML handoff (final-cut-pro)                               |
  | Design & illustration | Voyager's design engine when ready, for static design; without it, HTML/CSS/SVG rendered headless, Python imaging                               | Illustrator, Photoshop                                                           | type and logos are authored                                                        |
  | 3D                    | Blender; without it, no 3D tool: say so in one line                                                                                             |                                                                                  |                                                                                    |
  | Slides                | Voyager's design engine when ready, exporting PPTX and PDF; without it python-pptx for PPTX, HTML rendered to PDF                               |                                                                                  | PPTX opens in Keynote, PowerPoint and Google Slides; check it in the installed one |
  | Music & audio         | Voyager's audio engine when ready for composition; `make-music` for generated music routes; sound effects through `voyager`, mixing with FFmpeg |                                                                                  | voice cleanup with FFmpeg filters; Ableton Live and Logic Pro only when named      |

- **Another app's format wins:** when the input or requested output is another
  app's format (`.aep`, `.prproj`, `.drp`, `.ai`, `.psd`, `.als`, `.logicx`, and
  so on), work in that app and return the format the user gave.

### Asking for another app's name

"Make it in Keynote" or "a PowerPoint" names a tool, so it wins: drive
that app when it is installed, and change a native file they hand you in its
app. When it isn't installed, or they name Google Slides, build the PPTX with
python-pptx (PPTX for Keynote, PowerPoint and Google Slides import; PDF when
they only need to present or send it).

## Typography

For authoring text or changing fonts, layout or output size.

- Author exact words, numbers and supplied logos as controlled text or overlays;
  inspect the exported file rather than relying on generated imagery to spell.

- Verify the actual renderer has the faces you use; a brand kit's supported-font
  flag is not proof of availability.

- Protect descenders,
  accents and cap height from clipping, including inside masks and line boxes.

- Use the editor integration skill for font loading. For a brand's fonts in Remotion or
  HyperFrames that is the generated brand-fonts helper, not hand-written `@font-face`;
  if it reports a substitute, say so to the user.

- Renderers add no motion blur: fine print and 1–2 px hairlines shimmer in fast moves; keep them out of fast moves or enlarge them.

## A pet’s 3D body

For a 3D pet, `model.file` in `pet.json` is a rigged GLB with named animation clips and `EXT_meshopt_compression`; tools that cannot read that extension need the model decompressed first.
